newsitem.title: USA: Fed expected to refrain from operations.
newsitem.headline: Fed expected to refrain from operations.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to refrain from open market operations on Tuesday, analysts said.

"We're looking for no operations," said Waldo Best, senior economist at BZT Securities. "They did seven-day systems last week and the one-day systems from yesterday means they are pretty much done for the week. The tax pressure (from Monday's tax date) is over for now."
Best said the Fed's add need next week is pretty large but said, "They can handle it doing these seven-day systems. We're looking for another one of those on Thursday."

"We expect no action but there's a chance of the Fed (adding reserves through) customer repurchases if the Fed funds rate increases," said Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities America Inc.
At 0907 EDT/1307 GMT, Fed funds were trading at 5-3/16 percent, just below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.
-- Ellen Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679
